scope: Proposition 9.5 (Transport of constants) of the manuscript “Filtered chromatic splitting at generic primes” (preprints/Filtered-chromatic-splitting-at-generic-primes-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f2aeefc98af1afcd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The structural maps from (9.5) identify H∗ (Pn, Fp) ∼ − − → H∗ (Mn, Fp)(1) ∼ ← − − H∗ (Jn, Fp), (9.6) where (1) denotes generalized eigenvalue one for γ. These are identifications by the actual pullback maps and preserve cup products. Together with Lemma 9.3, they induce natural equivalences, for every finite Postnikov p-primary spectrum E, C∗ cts(Pn; E) ≃ C∗ (Mn; E)(1) ≃ C∗ cts(Jn; E) ≃ C∗ cts(Kn; E). (9.7) The equivalences commute with coefficient maps, products, and Hurewicz maps. They extend to the p-complete sphere by the Postnikov and coefficient limits defining continuous cochains. There is also the following compatibility on the independent extension locus Z = (Nm t )ind, m = n − t. After fixing the connected quotient frame, let b : [Z/Km] −→ BPn, q : [Z/Km] −→ BKm be the positive middle-bundle classifying map and the structural map. If cP and cK correspond under (9.7), then b∗ cP = q∗ resKn Km (cK), Km −→ Kn, g 7−→ diag(g, 1t). (9.8) This equality holds for finite Postnikov coefficients, for their stable limits, and for the resulting ordinary cup actions. In particular the constant action in Proposition 8.3 is the actual block- restriction action.
